1. Scope — Covers the main dimensions of endless hexagonal belts, generally intended for use on 
agricultural machinery ( specially on harvester-thresher machines ), togetherwith the groove sections of 
the corresponding fixed diameter pulleys. 

2. Dimensions —As given in Table 1.

2.1 Belts — An endless hexagonal belt on an agricultural machine transmits a high degree of force 
per unit of section; when it approaches a groove pulley, its cross-section undergoes, as a result, 
appreciable deformation. For this reason the various dimensions which are defined hereunder are to be 
taken as being those of the belt placed on the device used for the measurement of its length and 
subjected to the measuring force F. The dimensions W and T are those relating to the parts of the beit 
when in contact with the measuring pulleys (see Fig. in Table 1 and 3). 

2.1.1 Cross-sect/on {see Table 1 ) — The theoretical profile of these belts is a hexagon consisting 
of two equal isosceles trapezia joined at their wider base; the neutral axis, coinciding in practice with 
the transverse diagonal of this hexagon, is located therefore at half the height of the section.

Note — Reduced length tolerances may be used with the agreement of manufacturer and indentor. 

2.1.3 Tolerance on length — The length of the belts is affected by the maximum admissible 
deviations of + p/2 and — p, where p is calculated, with a certain amount of approximation, using the 
formula: 

p = 0'8 vT + 0'006£ 

L being the preferred number from the R 10 series equal to or immediately greater than the 
effective length, expressed in millimetres. 



2.2 Pulleys 

2.2.1 Pulleys having parallel axes of rotation — The hexagonal belts can be used with pulley 
profiles in accordance with IS:3142-1982 'Specification for V-grooved pulleys for V-belts groove, 
Sections A, B, C, D & E (first revision)'. 



IS: 11038- 1984 



Section 


Grooved Pulley for 


A 


HAA belts

HBB belts

HCC belts 


D 


HDD belts 



2.2.2 Pulleys whose axes of rotation are not parallel — In such cases, it is often necessary to 
increase the outside diameter of the pulley in relation to the effective diameter, and sometimes the 
angle of the groove in order to allow the belts to approach and leave the grooves without friction 
occurring with their edges. 

It is not possible to determine any outline of groove which would suit all cases of transmission 
between shafts that are not parallel. However, certain national specifications define the geometrical 
characteristics that govern transmission between orthogonal shafts (known as quarter-turn drives) and 
particularly the special groove profile (known as 'deep groove') to be used in this case. 

3. Measurement of Length of Belts 

3.1 Principle of Measurement — The device recommended, shown in sketch form in Table 3, consists 
essentially of two grooved pulleys of similar functional dimensions, one of which is movable in the 
same plane as the belt by the measuring force F ( see Table 3 ). Rotate the belt to make at least two 
complete revolutions of the belt, then measure the distance E between centres of the two pulleys.

3.2 Calculation of Length — The effective length of the belt, that is, the length measured at the level 
of its effective width Uu is obtained from the formula: 

4ff 2£= + C ef f 
C e ff indicating the effective circumference of the control pulleys ( see Table 3 •). 

3.3 Groove-Section of Measurement Pulleys — Only the values of f e it of C e u and of the angle of the 
groove a are of importance; the depth h in Table 3 is given only for information. 

4. Relation Between Effective Diameter and Pitch Diameter ( see Fig. 1 ) — The pitch diameter 
dp of V-belt pulleys, as defined in IS : 3142-1982 and the corresponding effective diameter d e u when 
these pulleys are used with hexagonal belts are connected by the following formula: 

tfeff = dp + 2Y 

the values of factor Y being as given by Table 4.

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard is based on ISO 5289-1978 'Endless hexagonal belts for agricultural machinery and 
groove sections of corresponding pulleys' issued by the International Organization for Standardization 
(ISO).
